comparisons.peer_topic: Customer and other payables composition and valuation
comparisons.peer_summary: As of December 2024, customer and other payables totaled $223.26 billion, primarily consisting of customer credit balances from prime brokerage activities, and are accounted for at cost plus accrued interest which approximates fair value.
comparisons.comparison: Both Bank of America and Goldman Sachs disclose specific cash deposits or payables associated with clearing organizations, though they categorize them differently on the balance sheet. BAC reports $21.5 billion in cash deposited with clearing organizations primarily in other assets. In contrast, GS reports $6.11 billion in payables to brokers, dealers, and clearing organizations (a liability) within its customer and other payables, while its total customer payables are $217.15 billion. This indicates BAC focuses on the asset side (deposits made) for this specific metric, while GS highlights the liability side (payables due) for clearing entities within its broader prime brokerage activities.

sentences.text: In addition, at December 31, 2024 and 2023, the Corporation had cash deposited with clearing organizations of $21.5 billion and $23.7 billion primarily recorded in other assets on the Consolidated Balance Sheet.

Customer and other payables included payables to customers and counterparties of $217.15 billion as of December 2024 and $220.71 billion as of December 2023, and payables to brokers, dealers and clearing organizations of $6.11 billion as of December 2024 and $10.02 billion as of December 2023.

comparisons.peer_topic: Other Restricted Assets Including Pledged Cash and Securities
comparisons.peer_summary: As of December 31, 2024 and 2023, the Firm had $40.7 billion and $40.5 billion in cash and securities pledged with clearing organizations, and $26.8 billion and $20.5 billion in restricted securities related to customer activity, respectively.
comparisons.comparison: Bank of America and JPMorgan Chase both disclose cash held with clearing organizations as restricted or pledged assets. BAC had $21.5 billion in cash deposited with clearing organizations recorded in other assets. JPM had $40.7 billion in cash and securities pledged with clearing organizations for the benefit of customers. Both amounts represent significant cash/asset reserves maintained for clearing activities, though JPM explicitly includes securities in the pledged amount and attributes it to customer benefit, whereas BAC simply lists it as cash deposits in other assets.

sentences.text: In addition, at December 31, 2024 and 2023, the Corporation had cash deposited with clearing organizations of $21.5 billion and $23.7 billion primarily recorded in other assets on the Consolidated Balance Sheet.
• Cash and securities pledged with clearing organizations for the benefit of customers of $40.7 billion and $40.5 billion, respectively.

comparisons.peer_summary: Cash and cash equivalents also include restricted cash, such as cash segregated to comply with federal or other regulations including minimum reserve requirements, and initial margin deposited with clearing organizations.
comparisons.comparison: Bank of America and Morgan Stanley both identify cash deposited with clearing organizations as a component of restricted cash or cash equivalents. BAC reports $21.5 billion in cash deposited with clearing organizations primarily in other assets. MS includes the Firm's initial margin deposited with clearing organizations as part of its restricted cash within cash and cash equivalents. Both disclosures link clearing organization deposits to restricted or segregated cash status, reflecting regulatory or operational constraints on that liquidity.
